newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's Madani said to reject order on politics. [CORRECTED 14:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Algeria's Madani said to reject order on politics. [CORRECTED 14:35 GMT]

text.p: Algeria's radical Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) chief Abassi Madani, freed 13 days ago from jail, has rejected a government order to refrain from political activity, an Arabic newspaper said on Monday.

"I have knowledge that the man refused to sign conditions outlined by the interior minister in his last statement and that Madani refused to abide by the minister's decision on that," said the Egyptian newspaper Al Ahram, quoting Islamist leader Abdallah Djaballah.
(Corrects name and location of newspaper quoting Islamist leader).
Djaballah, head of the legal Islamist Nahda party seen as close to the FIS, urged the authorities to allow Madani to be a fully free to help end Algeria's violence.
The conflict between Moslem rebels and the government has raged since 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which the now outlawed FIS had taken a huge lead.
About 60,000 people have died since then.

Interior Minister Mustapha Ben Mansour angrily ordered Madani, three days after his release on parole on July 15, to abstain from making statements and other political activities without prior authorisation from the minister.
Madani had said he and his supporters would do all they could to end the violence shaking the North African country.
He was arrested in June 1991 and sentenced a year later by a military court to 12 years jail for threatening state security. He was set free halfway through his jail sentence.
